tweet.text:
I used grok-cli (Yes, there is a CLI -- look it up) for a week or so.  I was both impressed and horrified.  It was able to help me a great deal -- especially with refactorings.  But it was sloppy about parentheses (this is clojure after all) and concurrency, and several other issues.  I think it made me 10%-20% more productive.

After one day of using Claude (Yes, I heard all of you out there in the peanut gallery) I am both impressed and horrified.

I am impressed that it has a much better grasp of the code than grok.  It's not _as_ sloppy with the basics.  But it still makes dumb mistakes and piles code on top of code.  The code it writes is better than grok's by a small margin; but I still need to guide it in refactoring and cleanup.  No way am I giving it a free hand to ride roughshod over the code!

My biggest horror is the time and cost.  Claude is noticeably slower than grok, and it costs at least ten times what grok costs.  The time it takes is reminiscent of compiles in the 90's.  As for the cost, If I were to use Claude as a full time assistant I think it could cost me several hundred dollars a month, whereas grok would likely cost me less than $20.  

I'm not ready to do a bottom line yet; but if one day counts as experience then I think Claude has increased my productivity by another 10%-20% over grok.  If that holds true then the cost is dwarfed by the productivity gain.
